title: The Wrong Change at the Fish Market
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Every Saturday morning, I buy fish from the same stall at the wet market, mostly because the seller remembers exactly how I like it cleaned.
Narrator: [reflective] Last week, however, something small happened that I have not stopped thinking about since, even though it lasted less than a minute.
Narrator: [honestly] The seller was rushing, because the queue behind me was long, and when she handed back my change, she counted too quickly.
Narrator: [with feeling] I did not realize the mistake until I was already walking away, and once I checked my pocket, I saw she had given me almost double what I was owed.
Narrator: [thoughtful] If I had simply kept walking, nobody would have noticed, and she would have blamed herself later, assuming she noticed at all.
Narrator: [honestly] For a moment, I actually considered it, because this month has been tight, and that extra money would have covered my bus fare for a week.
Narrator: [determined] Still, I turned around and walked back through the crowd, even though it meant losing my place near the front of the queue.
Narrator: [gently] When I explained the mistake, she looked surprised, and then almost embarrassed, as if she assumed most customers would have simply kept it without a second thought.
Narrator: [reflective] She tried to give me a small discount next time as a thank you, but I told her that wasn't necessary, and that returning it wasn't a favor to her.
Narrator: [thoughtful] What struck me afterward was how ordinary it felt, even though the choice underneath it was not small at all.
Narrator: [honestly] Nobody would have judged me for keeping it, and in fact, nobody would have even known there was a decision to make.
Narrator: [sincere] That is exactly why it mattered to me, because the only witness to what I chose was the one I was doing it for in the first place.
Narrator: [peacefully] I still think about how easily I could have justified keeping it, telling myself it was her mistake, not mine, and that I deserved a little help this month.
Narrator: [warmly] In spite of that temptation, I am glad I turned around, because some choices only matter precisely when no one is watching except yourself.

quiz.question: What mistake did the fish seller make?
options: She gave the narrator the wrong fish
She gave the narrator almost double the correct change
She overcharged the narrator
She forgot to clean the fish
quiz.explanation: The seller counted too quickly and gave back almost double what the narrator was actually owed.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator briefly consider keeping the extra money?
options: She wanted revenge on the seller
This month has been financially tight and the money would help
She thought the seller was rich
She didn't like the seller
quiz.explanation: She admits the month has been financially tight and the extra money would have covered her bus fare.

quiz.question: What did the narrator do after realizing the mistake?
options: She kept walking and said nothing
She turned around and walked back to return the money
She called the market manager
She left the money at the stall without explaining
quiz.explanation: She turned around and walked back through the crowd, even though it meant losing her place in the queue.

quiz.question: How did the seller react when the narrator explained the mistake?
options: She was angry
She looked surprised and almost embarrassed
She refused to believe it
She ignored the narrator
quiz.explanation: The seller looked surprised, and then almost embarrassed, assuming most customers would have kept the money.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator say the moment mattered to her?
options: Because everyone was watching her
Because the only witness to her choice was the one she was doing it for
Because she wanted a discount
Because she wanted to be praised publicly
quiz.explanation: She says the moment mattered because the only witness to her decision was the one she was doing it for in the first place.

title: The Invoice That Favored Us by Mistake
script: Bagas: [curious] Mira, did you check the supplier's invoice this month? Something looks strange to me.
Mira: [thoughtful] I glanced at it earlier. Why, did the total seem off to you as well?
Bagas: [carefully] They billed us for three hundred units, but I'm fairly sure we actually received closer to four hundred and fifty.
Mira: [surprised] Are you sure? If that's true, we've been undercharged for weeks, not just this month.
Bagas: [honestly] I checked our warehouse records twice already, and the numbers don't match at all, so I don't think it's my mistake.
Mira: [hesitant] Honestly, part of me wants to just stay quiet about it. Our budget has been stretched thin since the new project started.
Bagas: [understanding] I get that completely, and believe me, I thought about staying quiet too, even if only for a moment.
Mira: [thoughtful] However, if we say nothing and they eventually notice their own error, we'll look like we deliberately let it slide.
Bagas: [gently] That's not even the main reason for me, though. Even if they never noticed, we would still know exactly what happened.
Mira: [reflective] You're right. As a result, staying silent would essentially mean deciding to keep money that was never actually ours.
Bagas: [determined] Exactly. So I think we should contact them directly, explain the discrepancy, and offer to pay the corrected amount.
Mira: [worried] What if they think we're only saying something now because we're worried about getting caught later?
Bagas: [calmly] That's possible, but their opinion of our intentions isn't really something we can control either way.
Mira: [thoughtful] True. Despite the risk of looking suspicious, doing the right thing shouldn't depend on how it might be interpreted.
Bagas: [warmly] Exactly my thinking. Besides, our supplier has always treated us fairly, even when shipments were delayed on our side.
Mira: [sincere] Okay, let's draft the email together this afternoon, and I'll ask finance to recalculate the correct balance before we send it.
Bagas: [relieved] Thank you for agreeing so quickly. I was a little worried you'd want to wait until next quarter instead.
Mira: [smiling] No, if something's wrong, it's better fixed now, even though it costs us more this month than we planned for.

quiz.question: What did Bagas notice about the supplier's invoice?
options: It was for the wrong company
They were billed for fewer units than they actually received
The prices had doubled
The invoice was missing entirely
quiz.explanation: Bagas noticed they were billed for three hundred units but had actually received closer to four hundred and fifty.

quiz.question: Why does Mira initially want to stay quiet about it?
options: She dislikes the supplier
Their budget has been stretched thin since a new project started
She thinks it's not their responsibility
She doesn't believe Bagas
quiz.explanation: Mira admits their budget has been stretched thin, so part of her wants to stay quiet.

quiz.question: What does Bagas say matters more than whether the supplier notices?
options: Getting a reward for honesty
Knowing what happened even if the supplier never notices
Avoiding paperwork
Impressing their manager
quiz.explanation: Bagas says that even if the supplier never noticed, they would still know exactly what happened.

quiz.question: What do Mira and Bagas decide to do?
options: Ignore the mistake completely
Contact the supplier, explain the discrepancy, and offer to pay the corrected amount
Wait until next quarter to mention it
Ask a lawyer to intervene
quiz.explanation: Bagas suggests contacting the supplier directly and offering to pay the corrected amount, and Mira agrees.

quiz.question: How does Mira respond to the risk of looking suspicious?
options: She decides it's better to say nothing
She says doing the right thing shouldn't depend on how it might be interpreted
She blames Bagas for the situation
She asks to delay the decision indefinitely
quiz.explanation: Mira concludes that despite the risk of looking suspicious, doing the right thing shouldn't depend on interpretation.

title: The Neighbor I Visit Without Telling Anyone
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] There is an elderly man who lives two doors down from me, and for the past year, I have been visiting him twice a week.
Narrator: [reflective] His children moved abroad long ago, and although they call occasionally, he spends most of his days completely alone in that quiet house.
Narrator: [honestly] I started visiting almost by accident, after I noticed his newspaper piling up uncollected by the gate for several days in a row.
Narrator: [gently] At first, I only knocked to check if he was alright, but eventually those short visits turned into something closer to a habit I looked forward to.
Narrator: [thoughtful] If someone asked my wife what I do on Tuesday and Friday evenings, she genuinely wouldn't know how to answer in detail.
Narrator: [honestly] I never mentioned it to her, not because I'm hiding anything shameful, but because explaining it out loud would somehow make it feel smaller.
Narrator: [reflective] Even my closest friends assume those evenings are simply my time for errands, and I've never bothered correcting that assumption.
Narrator: [with feeling] Sometimes we just sit together in silence, drinking tea, while he tells the same three stories about his youth that I've already heard many times.
Narrator: [warmly] I don't mind hearing them again, though, because his face changes completely whenever he talks about those years, as if he becomes younger while speaking.
Narrator: [thoughtful] A colleague once suggested I post about it online, arguing it might inspire other people to check on their own elderly neighbors.
Narrator: [honestly] I understood his point, and perhaps it really would encourage someone else, but something about the suggestion still felt wrong to me.
Narrator: [reflective] If I photographed those visits for others to see, I suspect I would start visiting partly for the photograph, without even realizing the shift.
Narrator: [sincere] So instead, I keep it quiet, unrecorded, and mostly unmentioned, even though nobody would think less of me for sharing it.
Narrator: [peacefully] As long as he keeps opening that door glad to see me, I don't need anyone else to know these evenings ever happened at all.

quiz.question: How did the narrator first start visiting his elderly neighbor?
options: The neighbor asked him directly
He noticed the newspaper piling up uncollected by the gate
A mutual friend introduced them
The neighbor's children asked him
quiz.explanation: He started after noticing the newspaper piling up uncollected by the gate for several days.

quiz.question: Why hasn't the narrator told his wife the details of his Tuesday and Friday evenings?
options: He is hiding something shameful
Explaining it out loud would somehow make it feel smaller
His wife told him not to mention it
He forgot to tell her
quiz.explanation: He says it's not because he's hiding anything shameful, but explaining it out loud would make it feel smaller.

quiz.question: What do the narrator and the elderly man usually do during visits?
options: Watch television together
Sit in silence drinking tea while the man repeats old stories
Go for long walks
Cook meals together
quiz.explanation: They sit together drinking tea while the man tells the same three stories about his youth.

quiz.question: What did a colleague suggest the narrator do?
options: Stop visiting the neighbor
Post about the visits online to inspire others
Charge the neighbor for his time
Bring other neighbors along
quiz.explanation: A colleague suggested posting about it online, arguing it might inspire others to check on elderly neighbors.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator reject that suggestion?
options: He was too busy to post online
He suspected he would start visiting partly for the photograph
He didn't have social media
He thought no one would care
quiz.explanation: He suspected that if he photographed the visits, he would start visiting partly for the photograph without realizing it.

title: A Debate About Posting the Donation Video
script: Reza: [excited] Tasya, I filmed us handing out the food packages this morning. Should we post it on the community page tonight?
Tasya: [hesitant] I'm not sure, honestly. Something about posting it makes me a little uncomfortable, even though I can't fully explain why yet.
Reza: [reasonable] But if we post it, more people might join next month, and the families waiting for help would benefit directly.
Tasya: [thoughtful] That's a fair point, and I understand the logic completely. However, I keep wondering whose comfort we're actually prioritizing here.
Reza: [curious] What do you mean by that exactly?
Tasya: [gently] I mean, did anyone in that video actually agree to be filmed while receiving help in front of their neighbors?
Reza: [pausing] Honestly, no, nobody asked them directly. We were focused on capturing the moment, not on asking permission first.
Tasya: [reflective] Even if the video brings more donations later, receiving charity in public can feel humiliating, no matter how kindly it's filmed.
Reza: [considering] I hadn't thought about it from their side at all, only from ours, in terms of visibility and future support.
Tasya: [warmly] I'm not saying we should never document anything we do, but this particular video crosses a line I'm not comfortable with.
Reza: [thoughtful] What if we blurred their faces, or filmed only the boxes being packed, without showing anyone actually receiving them?
Tasya: [relieved] That would change things completely, since it would tell people what we're doing without exposing anyone's private moment of need.
Reza: [determined] Alright, let's re-edit it tonight then, and next time, I'll ask everyone beforehand if they're comfortable being filmed at all.
Tasya: [sincere] Thank you for being willing to reconsider, even though I know you filmed it with genuinely good intentions in mind.
Reza: [honestly] I think I got caught up in wanting people to see our effort, rather than thinking carefully about the people we were actually helping.
Tasya: [gently] That happens easily, especially when the cause itself is good. It's worth pausing occasionally to ask who a post is really for.
Reza: [warmly] Agreed. Let's finish the edited version, and this time, we'll ask first instead of explaining ourselves afterward.

quiz.question: What did Reza film that morning?
options: A community meeting
Them handing out food packages
A fundraising concert
A cooking class
quiz.explanation: Reza filmed them handing out food packages to families that morning.

quiz.question: Why is Tasya uncomfortable posting the video?
options: The video quality is poor
Nobody in the video agreed to be filmed while receiving help publicly
She doesn't like Reza's editing
She thinks it's illegal
quiz.explanation: Tasya points out that nobody in the video actually agreed to be filmed while receiving help in front of their neighbors.

quiz.question: What does Tasya say about receiving charity in public?
options: It always feels great for everyone
It can feel humiliating, no matter how kindly it's filmed
It doesn't matter how it's filmed
Only wealthy people mind
quiz.explanation: She says receiving charity in public can feel humiliating, no matter how kindly the video is filmed.

quiz.question: What compromise do Reza and Tasya agree on?
options: Delete the video entirely and never document anything
Re-edit the video to show only boxes being packed, without showing anyone receiving them
Post the video exactly as filmed
Ask a stranger to appear in the video instead
quiz.explanation: They agree to re-edit the video to show only the boxes being packed, without exposing anyone's private moment of need.

quiz.question: What does Reza realize about his own motivation?
options: He filmed it to embarrass the families
He got caught up in wanting people to see their effort rather than thinking of those they helped
He never wanted to help at all
He was forced to film it
quiz.explanation: Reza admits he got caught up in wanting people to see their effort, rather than thinking carefully about the people they were helping.

title: Telling the Truth About the Gap on My Resume
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Last month, I sat across from an interviewer who kept staring at the eighteen-month gap on my resume, clearly waiting for an explanation.
Narrator: [reflective] A friend of mine had suggested, beforehand, that I simply say I was traveling, since that answer sounds confident and requires no further questions.
Narrator: [honestly] The truth, however, was that I left my previous job to care for my mother after her diagnosis, and I nearly didn't recover financially from that decision.
Narrator: [thoughtful] If I told the traveling story, the interview would likely move on smoothly, and nobody would ever question it further.
Narrator: [determined] Even so, sitting there, I decided I would rather explain the real reason and risk an awkward silence than build the job on a comfortable lie.
Narrator: [honestly] So I explained it plainly, that my mother needed full-time care, and that I chose her over my career during that period without much hesitation.
Narrator: [with feeling] The interviewer paused for a moment, and I genuinely couldn't tell whether that silence meant judgment or simply surprise at my directness.
Narrator: [reflective] Then she said something I didn't expect, that she respected people who choose family over convenience, even when it costs them professionally.
Narrator: [warmly] We ended up talking for several extra minutes about caregiving, and the entire tone of the interview shifted into something far more genuine.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I don't know yet if I got the position, and honestly, the honest answer might still work against me with a different interviewer.
Narrator: [determined] However, I realized that if a company only wants me because of a comfortable story, then it isn't really a place I want to work for long.
Narrator: [sincere] I would rather be hired, or rejected, for exactly who I am and what I chose, than build a career on a small, convenient lie repeated for years.
Narrator: [peacefully] Despite the uncertainty, I walked out of that interview feeling steadier than I expected, as though I had finally stopped performing for a stranger's approval.
Narrator: [warmly] Whatever the outcome turns out to be, at least this time, whoever hires me will actually know the person they are hiring.

quiz.question: What was the interviewer curious about?
options: Her salary expectations
An eighteen-month gap on her resume
Her educational background
Her reference letters
quiz.explanation: The interviewer kept staring at the eighteen-month gap on her resume, waiting for an explanation.

quiz.question: What had a friend suggested she say about the gap?
options: That she was fired
That she was traveling
That she was studying abroad
That she was ill
quiz.explanation: A friend suggested she simply say she was traveling, since it sounds confident and avoids further questions.

quiz.question: What was the real reason for the gap?
options: She was traveling
She left her job to care for her mother after a diagnosis
She was unemployed by choice
She was starting a business
quiz.explanation: She left her previous job to care for her mother after her diagnosis.

quiz.question: How did the interviewer respond to the honest explanation?
options: She ended the interview immediately
She said she respected people who choose family over convenience
She accused the narrator of lying
She refused to discuss it further
quiz.explanation: The interviewer said she respected people who choose family over convenience, even when it costs them professionally.

quiz.question: What conclusion does the narrator reach about honesty in the interview?
options: She regrets telling the truth
She would rather be hired or rejected for who she actually is than build a career on a lie
She plans to lie next time instead
She thinks honesty never matters in interviews
quiz.explanation: She concludes she would rather be hired or rejected for exactly who she is than build a career on a convenient lie.

title: A Podcast About the Tuition Fee Nobody Could Explain
script: Host: [warmly] Tonight's guest is Arman, a university administrator with an unusual story about a tuition payment. Welcome, Arman.
Guest: [pleasantly] Thanks for having me. This story genuinely surprised our whole finance office when it happened.
Host: [curious] Set the scene for us. What exactly happened?
Guest: [thoughtful] A struggling student was one week away from being withdrawn for unpaid fees, despite having excellent grades throughout the semester.
Guest: [reflective] Then, seemingly out of nowhere, her entire remaining balance was paid in cash, in person, by someone our staff didn't recognize at all.
Host: [interested] Did that person leave any information behind, a name, a note, anything at all?
Guest: [honestly] Nothing. He simply said the payment was for her account, insisted on no receipt with his name, and left before anyone could ask further questions.
Host: [surprised] How did the student react when she found out?
Guest: [warmly] She came into our office in tears, asking desperately who had paid it, because she wanted to thank them properly, even just once.
Host: [thoughtful] Could you tell her anything useful?
Guest: [gently] Only that he was an older man, calm, and that he asked our cashier not to make a scene about it whatsoever.
Host: [curious] Do you have any theory about who he might have been?
Guest: [reflective] We suspect he may have overheard her talking with a friend in the hallway about being withdrawn, although we can't confirm that at all.
Host: [thoughtful] What strikes you most about this story, even now?
Guest: [sincere] That in spite of having every opportunity to be thanked publicly, he clearly chose not to be, on purpose, deliberately.
Host: [reflective] It makes you wonder how often that happens quietly, without anyone in a story like this ever finding out.
Guest: [warmly] Exactly. We assume most tuition problems get solved through scholarships or loans, yet apparently some get solved by strangers who want nothing in return.
Host: [thoughtful] Has the student managed to stay enrolled since then?
Guest: [smiling] She has, and she's graduating this year, still hoping that one day, somehow, she'll manage to properly thank him.

quiz.question: What situation was the student facing?
options: She was failing her classes
She was about to be withdrawn for unpaid fees despite excellent grades
She had lost her scholarship
She was transferring universities
quiz.explanation: She was one week away from being withdrawn for unpaid fees, despite having excellent grades.

quiz.question: How was her remaining balance paid?
options: Through a university scholarship
In cash, in person, by someone the staff didn't recognize
By her own family
Through an online transfer
quiz.explanation: Her entire remaining balance was paid in cash, in person, by someone the finance staff didn't recognize.

quiz.question: What did the man insist on before leaving?
options: A receipt with his full name
No receipt with his name, and no scene made about it
A public announcement
A meeting with the student
quiz.explanation: He insisted on no receipt with his name and asked the cashier not to make a scene about it.

quiz.question: What is the guest's theory about how the man knew about the student's situation?
options: The student contacted him directly
He may have overheard her talking about being withdrawn in the hallway
He read about it in the newspaper
A teacher told him
quiz.explanation: They suspect he may have overheard her talking with a friend in the hallway about being withdrawn.

quiz.question: What does the guest find most striking about the story?
options: How much money was involved
That the man chose not to be thanked publicly despite the opportunity
How quickly the payment was processed
That the student never found out
quiz.explanation: He finds it striking that despite every opportunity to be thanked publicly, the man deliberately chose not to be.

title: Caring for the Father Who Wasn't Always There
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] My father was rarely present when I was growing up, working long stretches away from home, and missing most birthdays and school events entirely.
Narrator: [reflective] When I became an adult, I told myself I owed him nothing beyond basic politeness, given how distant those early years had genuinely felt.
Narrator: [honestly] Then, two years ago, he became seriously ill, and suddenly there was no one else nearby who could reasonably take on his daily care.
Narrator: [thoughtful] If I had refused, people would have understood, considering everything he missed, and nobody would have openly blamed me for walking away.
Narrator: [determined] Even so, I moved him into my apartment, adjusted my work schedule around his appointments, and started learning how to manage his medications properly.
Narrator: [with feeling] Some mornings, resentment still surfaces unexpectedly, especially when I'm exhausted, and I catch myself wondering why I'm doing this for someone so often absent.
Narrator: [reflective] However, I remind myself that caring for him isn't really a reward I'm giving him for good fathering, since that was never how this obligation worked.
Narrator: [honestly] It's something I do because of who I want to remain, regardless of who he happened to be during those earlier years of my life.
Narrator: [gently] A friend once asked whether I had finally forgiven him, expecting a simple, satisfying answer to a genuinely complicated question.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I told her honestly that forgiveness and duty don't always arrive together, and that I'm still working through the first while fully practicing the second.
Narrator: [warmly] Some evenings, though, while helping him into bed, he'll say something small, thank you, or I'm sorry, and it briefly softens something old inside me.
Narrator: [reflective] I don't expect those moments to erase an entire childhood of absence, and I've stopped hoping they eventually will.
Narrator: [sincere] What matters more to me now is that when I stand before Allah one day, I will have done my part, whatever he did or failed to do with his.
Narrator: [peacefully] That thought alone gets me through the harder mornings, even the ones where forgiveness still feels frustratingly out of reach.

quiz.question: How did the narrator describe his father during his childhood?
options: Always present and attentive
Rarely present, working long stretches away from home
Strict but always home
Absent due to illness
quiz.explanation: The narrator says his father was rarely present, working long stretches away and missing most birthdays and school events.

quiz.question: What happened two years ago that changed things?
options: His father remarried
His father became seriously ill and needed daily care
His father moved abroad
His father retired comfortably
quiz.explanation: His father became seriously ill two years ago, and there was no one else nearby to take on his daily care.

quiz.question: Why does the narrator say he cares for his father, according to the script?
options: As a reward for good fathering
Because of who he wants to remain, regardless of who his father was
Because his father demanded it
Because he expects an inheritance
quiz.explanation: He says it isn't a reward for good fathering, but something he does because of who he wants to remain.

quiz.question: How does the narrator answer his friend's question about forgiveness?
options: He says he fully forgave his father long ago
He says forgiveness and duty don't always arrive together
He refuses to discuss it
He says he will never forgive his father
quiz.explanation: He tells his friend that forgiveness and duty don't always arrive together, and he is still working through forgiveness.

quiz.question: What thought helps the narrator through harder mornings?
options: That his father will eventually apologize fully
That he will have done his part before Allah, regardless of what his father did
That his friends approve of his choice
That the illness will end soon
quiz.explanation: He says what matters is that he will have done his part before Allah, whatever his father did or failed to do.
